(Search snippet content — Reuters wire copy syndicated; full article not fetched; Reuters' own reporting language)

The FTSE 100 closed up 0.26% at 10,722.07 points, while the FTSE 250 climbed 0.14%.
London's FTSE 100 rose on Thursday as strong profit growth at Shell lifted energy stocks. Shell rose 2.1% after the oil major reported its highest quarterly profit since 2022, and increased its share buyback program.
Energy stocks outperformed the broader market, with the sector climbing nearly 1.64% despite a dip in oil prices.
Haleon slid about 15%, its biggest one-day fall in its four years as a publicly listed firm, after the consumer health company cut its organic revenue growth forecast.
